Prison or President? Ace Magashule digs in

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Will Ace Magashule go to prison or the the Presidency

Unique Selling Point:
drama outside the magistrate court in Bloemfontein / a historical diary of Ace interviews and a one on one with his arch nemesis and former ally - Mxolisi Dukwana

Summary:
Tonight on Carte Blanche
As the RET forces mobilise for the final showdown between the Ramaphosa and Zuma/ Ace faction of the ANC, the secretary general has been quietly building support in the branches ahead of the next National General Council meeting later this year. What is his plan? Could he be our next president?

Summary
In 2018 Carte Blanche spoke to the former premier of the Free State Beatrice Maarshof about Ace Magashule. She had never spoken out before and her message was clear: “What Ace wants, Ace gets” she told Devi Sankaree Govender. Ace Magashule has been equally clear about his political intentions, when the Ramaphosa faction won at Nasrec in 2017 – Ace told supporters they would be back in five years. It looks as if he has been working very hard behind the scenes to ensure those predictions materialize. The ANC is divided – and supporters of Cyril Ramaphosa are asking is he is a lame duck president as Magashule and the former president defy the ANC and defy the president.



Further information:
But wait you say – there are 20 corruption charges against Magashule, isn’t Ace going to end up behind bars? Not necessarily, Ace has one of South Africa’s top legal minds – Lawrence Hodes in his corner and Hodes is supremely confident that his client will win his case. Perhaps, perhaps not- but the law is not always about justice. Its who has the better lawyer and time and again the state has blown its cases against those who loot our state with impunity.

Its high noon at the ok corral, and once again South Africa is on a precipice. The president promises a clean- up of corruption, but nothing happens, and his own secretary general tells reporters not to worry too much about the constitution while refusing to step aside as he faces corruption charges. On a second front, he is facing a defiant former president who has defied a constitutional court ruling and has mobilized a rag tag bunch of MKMVA soldiers to march outside NKANDLA – as a show of force to protect their former president. We speak to Dukwana, the RET forces on the ground outside the magistrate court and Mcebisi Ndletyana to find out which way the sands are shifting as South Africa finds itself in the midst of a crippling pandemic and economic meltdown.

ACE DIGS IN: FINAL SCRIPT FOR TX 28th FEB 2021 FACT CHECKED

Commentary One
The police arrived early to set up their barricades outside the Bloemfontein magistrates court. Large crowds were expected

This was the stage on the 19th February where the latest ANC political drama unfolded – another in a series, that frequently takes the country to the brink and back.

Up sound MK soldiers

The protagonists -Secretary General of the ruling party Ace Magashule, and Cyril Ramaphosa, president of the republic.

Vox Pop 1
We want to send a message to Cyril Ramaphosa. He must leave ACE alone

Commentary Two
Their titanic battle for the soul of the ANC, spilled out onto Bloemfontein’s streets where Magashule’s supporters were in a fighting mood

Up sound
isoldier! isoldier !

Commentary Three
In November 2020, Magashule was charged with 21 counts of corruption and fraud for his alleged role as the former premier of the Free State, in a R255 million rand asbestos eradication project.

ACE!! ACE!!

The project was meant to audit and later remove the asbestos rooftops on Free State township houses, and be complete by 2019

Millions were paid to politically connected companies. For his alleged role Magashule is also charged with money laundering. People got rich but the asbestos roofs remain, even today.

LINK
But for his supporters, these charges were not seen as an attempt to finally cleanse the ANC of corruption, but instead as a political hit from the Ramaphosa faction

Commentary Four
NEC member of the MK military veterans association, Carl Niehaus
Carl Niehaus
This is a political trial it is not a trial based on the fact that Comrade Ace had done anything criminally wrong.

Commentary Five
On the 19th February Magashule was summoned for a second appearance. He arrived early striding in, looking confident.
Journalist
How are you feeling Mr. Magashule?
Ace Magashule
I am like a fish in a river

Commentary six
It was easy to see why Magashule felt like a fish in the river. While he was inside the court, with the prosecution joining additional accused to the case, outside- behind the police lines, the crowds were firmly in Magashule’s corner

Do you think Mr. Magashule is innocent?
Supporter 1
Oh yes, but the court will prove that
Supporter 2
At the end of the day the truth will be known to the public. I don’t believe a man of his stature can be associated with wrong doing.

Commentary Seven
Professor of politics at UJ, Mcebisi Ndletyana is skeptical about the Bloemfontein crowds

Mcebisi
You have a lot of unemployed people, the ANC does this all the time, they give them money, they give them food, they give them fancy ANC shirts. the problem of a rented crowd is an established long standing problem within the ANC.

Commentary Eight
Mxolisi Dukwana, a former Ace ally and now one of his biggest detractors, knows Magashule well.

Mxolisi
Sometimes we confuse confidence with arrogance, especially when you don’t comprehend the magnitude of what you are facing. But the truth is he never expected to be where he is today. It is not confidence its arrogance

Commentary Nine
Despite the lockdown regulations, a stage had been erected where his supporters amassed, waiting for their political icon to leave court, and address them

Supporter on stage
We are Zuma, Zuma is us! We are Ace, Ace is us!



Commentary ten
If President Ramaphosa was paying attention – the message out of Bloemfontein was loud and clear- hands of Magashule, and Magashule for president of the country.

Supporter
The SG is going nowhere, the SG will stay until we are saying as the branches.
You want ACE to be president?
Exactly!
I am here today to support the incoming president of the Republic of SA, Ace Magashule

LINK
So Ace Magashule has presidential ambitions, but does he have a real shot at the top job? His supporters seem think so and certain journalists are beginning to consider the possibility.

This from the Daily Maverick’s Richard Poplak

There is magical thinking in polite South African society that ANC Secretary-General Ace Magashule’s political demise is imminent. In the real world, Ace is in the strongest position to wield the final, killing blow. He is perhaps the greatest threat democratic South Africa has ever faced.

Commentary eleven
Roy Jankielsohn, leader of the opposition in the Free State, has clashed with Magashule, and never underestimates him.

Roy Jankielsohn
Ace Magashule is an expert at manipulating internal ANC elective structures and controlling branches. He perfected this formula in the Free State and he has taken this formula to national level, where he has been doing exactly the same thing in Luthuli house. I don’t think it’s too alarmist or too unrealistic to imagine an Ace Magashule presidency in SA

Mcebisi Ndletyana
Laughs out loud. What the hell is Roy smoking?!

Commentary Twelve
Ndletyana says public outrage at corruption has in fact weakened Magashule

Ndletyana
But then you had money for sick people that were dying and it was an outrage, and Cyril Ramaphosa picked that up and used that public outrage to embolden his own position to strengthen himself within the ANC, and so ACE is now being swept away by that wave of outrage




Commentary thirteen
Magashule has a top legal team, but it’s still not a walk in the park for him. There are 16 accused including five companies, more than 70 counts of corruption in total, and more than 40 state witnesses. In August, the pretrial begins in the Bloemfontein high court

Mcebisi Ndletyana
There is a huge possibility that he will be convicted -even if he is not convicted his integrity will be in question. I mean are South Africans really that morally depraved that they would vote for someone like that?

LINK
In August 2020 the National executive committee of the ANC decided this:
“cadres of the ANC who are formally charged for corruption or other serious crimes must immediately step aside from all leadership positions in the ANC, legislatures or other government structures pending the finalization of their cases”

Commentary fourteen
But its 3 months since Ace Magashule was formally charged, and he has said he is going nowhere. On Friday he was chauffeured through the Bloemfontein streets in an Audi Q8

Up sound hooting

So how serious is the NEC about its own guidelines?

Mcebisi Ndletyana
Its imminent! Look this thing is going to come to a head at some point, and they will say we have finalized these guidelines -here you are! At that point he will be forced to say no I am not going anywhere. Then they are going to have to push him out!

Commentary fifteen
But why the delay if the ANC is serious about cleaning up corruption?

Mcebisi Ndletyana
This is not an easy subject for people to deal with because at some point they encouraged corruption. So corruption was a subculture in the ANC, so all of a sudden they have to act to clean themselves up! It’s not an easy thing, how far do you go? Someone might bring up my file! I might be next!

Commentary sixteen
It’s the 80 or so NEC members of the ANC that determine the top leadership of the country. Control the NEC, control the ANC, and you control the country, says Poplak. Is that what Magashule and his Radical Economic Transformation or RET supporters who oppose white monopoly capital, want?

Masa
His supporters are calling for a special General Conference, why would they want that?
Dukwana
They claim that they will then remove the president demonstrating how ill- informed some of these people who claim to be members of the ANC are. And you don’t have members of the ANC thinking they can’t go in as RET forces and just do as they want. It’s not going to happen

LINK
Meanwhile at Nkandla, another flank of the RET faction is giving President Ramaphosa a headache, as former president Jacob Zuma also digs in and defies a constitutional court order

Commentary seventeen
This week in a scathing affidavit, the state capture commission said Zuma should be sentenced to two years imprisonment because he intentionally and unlawfully failed to appear at the commission in February. However if he complies, they won’t execute on the warrant.

Mcebisi
Either way the republic wins, the issue is about accountability. If he shows up before Zondo and sits there for a grilling that alone is a sufficient win to hold him accountable to expose him. For us to celebrate as a democracy we need not necessarily need to see Zuma going to prison over this.

Commentary eighteen
So the storms are once again on the horizon of our political landscape as both Ace Magashule and Jacob Zuma face the full might of the law in the coming months.

THE END FINAL DURATION 10 00

PROMO ONE
Secretary general of the ANC Ace Magashule is facing charges of fraud and corruption – yet he has refused to step aside, despite a clear guidelines from the National executive committee

PROMO TWO
As Ace Magashule made a second appearance at the Bloemfontein magistrates court , his supporters message to President Ramaphosa was clear- Hands off, and Magashule for President

PROMO THREE
40 state witnesses, more than 70 charges and 16 accused. Will the asbestos eradication case be the end of Ace Magashule’s political career?
